issue_context.title: Angular component which references its own type and decorated by class decorator is broken when target es5 + enableIvy=true
comments:
Just realized that this issue was never fixed in 10.x version, only 11.x.
Would it be possible to merge this fix in 10.x version as well? A more recent issue that I reported was successfully merged in 10.2.x.

Thanks
Yes, I would have expected it to land on `10.2.x` but it was marked as targeting `rc` which resulted it only going in `master` and `11.0.x`. I'll check with @josephperrott and @crisbeto ...

Hi @ratoaq2 - I checked with the team. While this fix could have been merged into 10.2.x, that branch is now not the active patch branch. It is our standard policy to only backport security and catastrophic bugs to earlier branches. Please can I ask you to attempt an update to 11.0.x to receive the benefit of this fix?

Hi @petebacondarwin 

Unfortunately that's not a solution for us.
Our application belongs to a big enterprise ecosystem and we can't just move to Angular 11.
Isn't it possible to get this bug backported?

Thanks for the support

Unfortunately, even if this commit was merged to the 10.2.x branch, there is no planned release of that branch at this time. I would strongly advise pushing for your enterprise to update - which is good practice anyway since any other future bugs that are found would not be released on 10.2.x either.

A workaround for you could be to apply the patch locally to the [src/ngtsc/annotations/src/metadata.js](https://unpkg.com/browse/@angular/compiler-cli@10.2.3/src/ngtsc/annotations/src/metadata.js) as a postinstall step.

review_comments:
Note for reviewer: I'm not sure whether this won't end up being a bit too aggressive. In theory it could recurse down into a callback function and recreate an identifier that has the same name as the class being compiled. In practice that's very unlikely and even if it did happen, the emitted code should still be valid.

An alternate approach could be to move the `setClassMetadata` function into the component definition and have it be invoked by the runtime, but that will change the timing and won't allow for the call to be stripped away in production.
